focus: Exodus 36 sees the work on the tabernacle begin: Bezalel, Aholiab, and the skilled workers receive the offerings, and the people give so generously that Moses has to stop them. The artisans then make the curtains, coverings, frame, veil, and screen of the tabernacle just as the LORD had shown Moses in Exodus 26.

sections.title: The Work Begins and the People Must Be Told to Stop Giving
sections.summary: Bezalel, Aholiab, and every gifted artisan come to do the work and receive the offerings, while the people keep bringing freewill offerings every morning. When the craftsmen report, “The people bring much more than enough” (Exodus 36:5), Moses has it proclaimed that no one should bring more, for the material was sufficient for all the work, “indeed too much” (Exodus 36:7).

sections.title: The Curtains, Tent, and Coverings Are Made
sections.summary: The artisans weave ten curtains of fine linen with cherubim and join them with gold clasps, “that it might be one tabernacle” (Exodus 36:13). They make eleven curtains of goats’ hair joined with bronze clasps for the tent, and coverings of ram skins dyed red and badger skins.

sections.title: The Boards, Sockets, and Bars Are Made
sections.summary: Upright boards of acacia wood are made for the south, north, and west sides and the corners, set in silver sockets. Bars hold them together, with a middle bar running from end to end, and boards and bars are overlaid with gold.

sections.title: The Veil and the Screen for the Door Are Made
sections.summary: The veil is woven with cherubim and hung on four pillars overlaid with gold, set in silver sockets. The screen for the tabernacle door is woven by a weaver and hung on five pillars with gold-covered capitals and bronze sockets.

1.brief: Moses says that Bezalel, Aholiab, and every gifted artisan in whom the LORD has put wisdom “shall do according to all that the LORD has commanded.” The work is to follow God’s instructions exactly.
1.explain:
“And Bezalel and Aholiab, and every gifted artisan in whom the LORD has put wisdom and understanding, to know how to do all manner of work for the service of the sanctuary,”

Moses names the workers: “Bezalel and Aholiab” and every skilled worker whom “the LORD has put wisdom” in.

“shall do according to all that the LORD has commanded.”

The work is to follow God’s instructions exactly.

2.brief: Moses calls Bezalel, Aholiab, and every gifted artisan whose heart was stirred to come and do the work. Willing and skilled workers are summoned.
2.explain:
“Then Moses called Bezalel and Aholiab, and every gifted artisan in whose heart the LORD had put wisdom,”

Moses calls the craftsmen to begin.

“everyone whose heart was stirred, to come and do the work.”

The workers, like the givers, are those “whose heart was stirred.” Willing and skilled workers are summoned.

3.brief: The artisans receive from Moses all the offerings Israel brought, and the people keep bringing freewill offerings every morning. The giving continues day after day.
3.explain:
“And they received from Moses all the offering which the children of Israel had brought for the work of the service of making the sanctuary.”

The craftsmen receive the gifts from Moses.

“So they continued bringing to him freewill offerings every morning.”

The people keep giving “every morning.” The giving continues day after day.

4.brief: The craftsmen doing the work of the sanctuary come from their tasks. The workers stop to report something unusual.
4.explain:
“Then all the craftsmen who were doing all the work of the sanctuary came, each from the work he was doing,”

The craftsmen stop their work to report something unusual.

5.brief: The craftsmen tell Moses, “The people bring much more than enough for the service of the work which the LORD commanded us to do.” The people’s generosity exceeds what is needed.
5.explain:
“and they spoke to Moses, saying, ‘The people bring much more than enough for the service of the work which the LORD commanded us to do.”

The workers report that the people bring “much more than enough.” The gifts have exceeded the need for the work God commanded.

6.brief: Moses has it proclaimed through the camp that no one should bring any more, and the people are restrained from bringing. Moses must stop the giving.
6.explain:
“So Moses gave a commandment, and they caused it to be proclaimed throughout the camp, saying,”

Moses sends word through the whole camp.

“Let neither man nor woman do any more work for the offering of the sanctuary.’ And the people were restrained from bringing,”

Moses tells the people to stop. Generosity had to be held back.

7.brief: The material is sufficient for all the work, “indeed too much.” The willing hearts of the people have more than met the need.
7.explain:
“for the material they had was sufficient for all the work to be done—indeed too much.”

The material was “sufficient,” “indeed too much.” Moses stopped the collection because the gifts had met their purpose. Willing generosity and responsible stewardship belong together.

8.brief: The skilled artisans make ten curtains of fine linen in blue, purple, and scarlet, woven with cherubim. The building begins as God commanded in Exodus 26.
8.explain:
“Then all the gifted artisans among them who worked on the tabernacle made ten curtains woven of fine linen, and of blue, purple, and scarlet thread;”

The construction begins with “ten curtains,” as God commanded in 26:1.

“with artistic designs of cherubim they made them.”

The cherubim are woven in as instructed. The building follows God’s pattern exactly.
8.notes: Exodus 36:8–38 repeats almost word for word the instructions of 26:1–37, now in the past tense. The repetition shows that the willing gifts and the artisans’ skill served exactly what the LORD appointed. The explanations at 26:1–37 apply here.

9.brief: Each curtain is twenty-eight cubits long and four wide, all the same size. The measurements match God’s pattern.
9.explain:
“The length of each curtain was twenty-eight cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits; the curtains were all the same size.”

Each of the ten inner curtains is twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide, about 42 by 6 feet (26:2). Because all ten are the same size, the two sets of five match exactly, so the loops and clasps along their joining edges line up when the sets are fastened together (36:11–13).

10.brief: Five curtains are joined together and five together. The two sets are formed.
10.explain:
“And he coupled five curtains to one another, and the other five curtains he coupled to one another.”

Joining the curtains in two sets of five makes two large panels, each twenty cubits wide, which will be fastened together at the middle (26:3).

11.brief: Loops of blue yarn are made on the edges of the two sets. The curtains are prepared for joining.
11.explain:
“He made loops of blue yarn on the edge of the curtain on the selvedge of one set; likewise he did on the outer edge of the other curtain of the second set.”

The blue loops are sewn along the edge of the last curtain in each set, the two edges that will meet when the sets are joined (26:4).

12.brief: Fifty loops are made on each set to hold the curtains together. The work is precise.
12.explain:
“Fifty loops he made on one curtain, and fifty loops he made on the edge of the curtain on the end of the second set;”

Each set has fifty loops along its joining edge (26:5).

“the loops held one curtain to another.”

The loops on the two edges are set opposite one another, so each loop on one set faces a loop on the other, ready for a clasp.

13.brief: Fifty gold clasps couple the curtains together, “that it might be one tabernacle.” The dwelling is made one, as God intended.
13.explain:
“And he made fifty clasps of gold, and coupled the curtains to one another with the clasps, that it might be one tabernacle.”

Gold clasps join the curtains so that the dwelling is “one tabernacle” (26:6). Each clasp fastens a pair of facing loops, and together the fifty clasps make the two sets a single covering.

14.brief: Eleven curtains of goats’ hair are made for the tent over the tabernacle. The outer covering is made.
14.explain:
“He made curtains of goats’ hair for the tent over the tabernacle; he made eleven curtains.”

The eleven goats’ hair curtains form the tent, a covering spread over the inner linen curtains (26:7). Cloth of goats’ hair was strong and protected the finer curtains beneath it.

15.brief: Each goats’ hair curtain is thirty cubits long and four wide, all the same size. The measurements again match the pattern.
15.explain:
“The length of each curtain was thirty cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits; the eleven curtains were the same size.”

These curtains are thirty cubits long, two cubits longer than the inner curtains, so the goats’ hair tent can hang lower on each side and cover the linen curtains (26:8, 13).

16.brief: Five curtains are joined together and six together. The tent’s two sets are formed.
16.explain:
“He coupled five curtains by themselves and six curtains by themselves.”

One set has five curtains and the other six. The extra curtain lets part of the tent be doubled over at the front and the rest hang down at the back (26:9, 12).

17.brief: Fifty loops are made on the outer edge of each set. The tent is prepared for joining.
17.explain:
“And he made fifty loops on the edge of the curtain that is outermost in one set, and fifty loops he made on the edge of the curtain of the second set.”

As with the inner curtains, fifty loops line the joining edge of each set (26:10).

18.brief: Fifty bronze clasps join the tent together “that it might be one.” The outer tent is made one.
18.explain:
“He also made fifty bronze clasps to couple the tent together, that it might be one.”

The bronze clasps fasten the facing loops of the two goats’ hair sets, so the whole outer tent becomes one covering (26:11). Gold clasps join the inner curtains (36:13), while bronze serves for the outer tent.

19.brief: A covering of ram skins dyed red and a covering of badger skins are made for the tent. The outer layers are completed.
19.explain:
“Then he made a covering for the tent of ram skins dyed red, and a covering of badger skins above that.”

The two outer coverings, ram skins dyed red and badger skins above them, complete the roof and protect the tent (26:14).

20.brief: Upright boards of acacia wood are made for the tabernacle. The frame is built.
20.explain:
“For the tabernacle he made boards of acacia wood, standing upright.”

The upright boards of acacia wood form the frame that holds up the curtains (26:15). Acacia is a hard, durable wood that grows in the wilderness.

21.brief: Each board is ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide. The boards match God’s measurements.
21.explain:
“The length of each board was ten cubits, and the width of each board a cubit and a half.”

Each board is ten cubits tall, about 15 feet, and a cubit and a half wide, about 27 inches (26:16).

22.brief: Each board has two tenons for joining. The boards are made to fit together.
22.explain:
“Each board had two tenons for binding one to another. Thus he made for all the boards of the tabernacle.”

The two tenons are projecting pegs at the foot of each board. They fit into the sockets below (36:24) and keep the boards in line with one another (26:17).

23.brief: Twenty boards are made for the south side. The first long wall is built.
23.explain:
“And he made boards for the tabernacle, twenty boards for the south side.”

Twenty boards, each a cubit and a half wide, make the south wall about thirty cubits long (26:18).

24.brief: Forty silver sockets are made, two under each board. The silver foundation is laid.
24.explain:
“Forty sockets of silver he made to go under the twenty boards: two sockets under each of the boards for its two tenons.”

The sockets are heavy silver bases set on the ground. Each board has two tenons, so each needs two sockets, one for each tenon. Forty sockets under the twenty boards give the south wall a firm footing of silver (26:19), and each socket used a talent of silver (38:27).

25.brief: Twenty boards are made for the north side. The second long wall is built.
25.explain:
“And for the other side of the tabernacle, the north side, he made twenty boards”

The north wall matches the south wall, with twenty boards (26:20).

26.brief: Forty silver sockets are made for the north side, two under each board. Both long walls rest on silver.
26.explain:
“and their forty sockets of silver: two sockets under each of the boards.”

The north wall also stands on forty silver sockets, two under each board, so both long walls rest on silver (26:21).

27.brief: Six boards are made for the west side. The back wall is built.
27.explain:
“For the west side of the tabernacle he made six boards.”

Six boards form the west wall at the back of the tabernacle (26:22). The entrance was at the east end.

28.brief: Two boards are made for the back corners. The corners are strengthened.
28.explain:
“He also made two boards for the two back corners of the tabernacle.”

Two more boards are made for the back corners, where the west wall meets the two long walls (26:23).

29.brief: The corner boards are coupled together at the bottom and coupled together at the top by one ring. The corners hold the frame together.
29.explain:
“And they were coupled at the bottom and coupled together at the top by one ring. Thus he made both of them for the two corners.”

The corner boards are joined at the bottom and at the top by one ring, holding each corner firm and tying the back wall to the side walls (26:24).

30.brief: There are eight boards and sixteen silver sockets on the back wall. The foundation is complete.
30.explain:
“So there were eight boards and their sockets—sixteen sockets of silver—two sockets under each of the boards.”

Six boards and two corner boards make eight boards on the west side, standing on sixteen silver sockets (26:25).

31.brief: Bars of acacia wood are made, five for one side. The walls are braced.
31.explain:
“And he made bars of acacia wood: five for the boards on one side of the tabernacle,”

The bars run along the outside of the boards through gold rings (36:34), holding the upright boards together as one wall (26:26).

32.brief: Five bars are made for the other side and five for the west side. All three walls are braced.
32.explain:
“five bars for the boards on the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the tabernacle on the far side westward.”

Each of the three walls receives five bars (26:27). The east end was the entrance and had no boards.

33.brief: The middle bar is made to pass through the boards from end to end. The whole wall is bound together.
33.explain:
“And he made the middle bar to pass through the boards from one end to the other.”

The middle bar runs the full length of the wall, binding all the boards together (26:28).

34.brief: The boards and bars are overlaid with gold, with gold rings for the bars. The frame is finished with gold.
34.explain:
“He overlaid the boards with gold, made their rings of gold to be holders for the bars, and overlaid the bars with gold.”

The boards and bars are overlaid with gold, and the rings that hold the bars are made of gold (26:29). The frame is finished with gold.

35.brief: The veil is made of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen, worked with cherubim. The veil that will guard the Most Holy is made.
35.explain:
“And he made a veil of blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and fine woven linen; it was worked with an artistic design of cherubim.”

The veil that will guard the Most Holy Place is made as instructed (26:31). It is distinct from the screen at the door (36:37).

36.brief: Four pillars of acacia wood overlaid with gold, with gold hooks and silver sockets, are made for the veil. The veil’s supports are completed.
36.explain:
“He made for it four pillars of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold, with their hooks of gold; and he cast four sockets of silver for them.”

The veil hangs on four pillars overlaid with gold, standing on silver sockets (26:32).

37.brief: A screen for the tabernacle door is made of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen by a weaver. The entrance to the tent is prepared.
37.explain:
“He also made a screen for the tabernacle door, of blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and fine woven linen, made by a weaver,”

“A screen for the tabernacle door” is made (26:36). The entrance to the tent is prepared.

38.brief: Five pillars with hooks are made for the screen, their capitals and rings overlaid with gold and their sockets of bronze. The work on the parts of the tabernacle described in this section is finished.
38.explain:
“and its five pillars with their hooks.”

The screen’s “five pillars” are made.

“And he overlaid their capitals and their rings with gold, but their five sockets were bronze.”

The pillars have gold “capitals,” the tops of the pillars, and “bronze” sockets (26:37). The work on the tent itself is finished as God commanded.
